title: Code Review: Which Design Survives?
prompt: Two designs for the capstone storage layer are below. Write choose_design() returning "A" or "B" — the design that keeps the CLI testable and swappable. Then a comment line starting with # explaining why (one line, must mention the word 'storage' or 'layer').

tests.name: judgment call
tests.code:
_r = choose_design()
assert _r in ("A", "B"), f"answer A or B, got {_r!r}"
_lines = [l for l in code.splitlines() if l.strip().startswith("#") and ("storage" in l.lower() or "layer" in l.lower())]
assert _lines, "add the one-line # justification"
assert choose_design() == "B", "B keeps file I/O behind a seam the CLI never touches"
tests.hint: Design A: every menu action opens/reads/writes the file directly. Design B: the menu calls add/list functions that return data; one storage module does all I/O.
